content:
Goal
* Consider explaining each bitwise operation used in the contribution, e.g.

Assume [[x]] and [[y]] are bits:
• [[x]] {{AND}} [[y]] = 1 if [[x]] = [[y]] = 1; otherwise 0
• [[x]] {{OR}} [[y]] = 1 if [[x]] = 1 or [[y]] = 1; otherwise 0
• (and similarly for the other operators)

Input
* Please add "separated by a space" at the end.

Game modes
* Consider disabling Reverse mode. In that mode, players don't have access to the statement and may need to look up definitions online in order to complete the task.

Cases
* Please revise the cases so that:
  (a) the lengths of the binary numbers are similar between each test and its corresponding validator, and
  (b) different input lengths are covered in a balanced manner.
  
  Specifically:

  • NOR (test and validator): use binary numbers of around 13 to 18 digits

  • AND (validator): use binary numbers of around 20 digits

  • XNOR (test and validator): use binary numbers of around 25 to 30 digits

* Binary numbers with leading zeros are not adequately covered at the moment. Please make sure both tests and validators cover this situation, and [[a]] having leading zeros and [[b]] having leading zeros are equally covered.

* Additionally, please ensure that for every operator, all binary digit combinations appear in *both* the tests and validators, i.e. 0 op 0, 0 op 1, 1 op 0 and 1 op 1. Revise any existing cases where a combination is missing.

Thanks.

Thanks for the feedback!

I've applied all of your advices.

I'm a bit disappointed for the Reverse mode, since it is my favourite style of play, but I understand your reasons.

I've updated the constraints so that the maximum number for A and B is 2^25-1, and made each test case 4 digits longer than the previous one to cover all the range.

I've also tried to explain what is a bitwise operation in the Goal, but I'm unsure if it is clear enough.

Feel free to add remarks if you think it is needed!
